set.body:
The API reviewer audited all 78 export names. Recording the pattern and the worst cases; the full table is large and the pattern is the actionable part.

THE PATTERN. The names that pass are exactly the ones an fMRI person already owns: voxels, searchlights, regions, whole_brain, contrast, rdm, rsa, crossnobis, connectivity, as_neurovol. Everything ON THE PATH BETWEEN THEM - relation, compile_frame, cross_partitions, plan_geometry, geometry - is compiler vocabulary. So the user must learn five framework nouns in order to connect ten words they already knew. That is the whole naming problem in one sentence, and it explains why the package feels harder than it is: the unfamiliar terms are load-bearing for NAVIGATION even where they are not load-bearing for SEMANTICS.

WORST SINGLE OFFENDER: relation(). It is the data-entry function, the first thing anyone types, and it names a category-theoretic role rather than 'here are my run betas'. Suggested: effects() or run_effects().

SECOND WORST: the at= / over= argument pair. Not guessable in either direction. Confirmed that swapping them produces 'Frame fields are missing or noncanonical', which misdirects toward frame corruption - see bd-01KZY9B80RMYJD4QDAFS5ZBQSM, where it is the worst of the 986 error messages precisely because it is the most likely first mistake.

Representative suggestions, domain-facing:
  abstract_domain -> feature_space        compile_frame -> measure_at
  relation -> effects / run_effects       cross_partitions -> all_run_pairs
  lm_relation_fit -> glm_effects          evaluate_geometry -> query_effects
  geometry_alignment -> cka / rv_coefficient   (it IS CKA; the current name hides that)
  coherent_functional -> mean_pattern     measurement_form -> coupling
  reduce_partitions / aggregate_first -> average_after / average_before

TWO CASES WORTH SPECIAL ATTENTION.

  geometry_alignment is actively MISLEADING rather than merely opaque: it computes CKA, a
  named and widely known quantity, under a name that conceals it. Same class of loss as the
  geometry-versus-G problem on bd-01KZY96KKH0X14EC62S2VX2RV9.

  reduce_partitions / aggregate_first are two exports whose sole purpose is to name a stage
  ordering, and introduction.Rmd:241-246 is explicit that they name DIFFERENT ESTIMANDS and
  that neither is a hidden optimization for the other. So the distinction is Class II and must
  survive. But average_after / average_before states that distinction MORE plainly than the
  current names do. This is the one case where renaming makes a load-bearing distinction more
  visible rather than less, and it is worth doing for that reason rather than despite it.

SEQUENCING. Renames are deliberately NOT ranked highly. They are churn, they carry collision
risk - geometry renamed to effect_form would collide with the existing effect_form class - and
they buy less than tiering or error messages. Do them at the same time as the tiering work on
bd-01KZY8SFF6FW6N84Y424Z1JX9N, when the surface is being reorganised anyway, and not before.
set.title: Naming audit: the framework nouns sit exactly on the path between the domain words that already work
